'''Derrick Richard White'''              (born July 2, 1994)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derrick White Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whitede01.html |access-date=November 7, 2020 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=November 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112024321/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whitede01.html |url-status=live}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed "'''the Buffalo'''"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/derrick-white-leading-winning-charge-boston-celtics-smart-brown-injury-depth-buffalo-nba/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |title=Derrick White has taken his game to a new level for the Celtics - CBS Boston |website=[[CBS News]] |date=February 13, 2023}}</ref> or "'''the Swiss Army Knife'''" by his Celtics teammate [[Neemias Queta]], he played three years of [[college basketball]] in [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] for the [[UCCS Mountain Lions#Basketball|Colorado–Colorado Springs Mountain Lions]] before transferring to [[NCAA Division I|Division I]]'s [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]] for his final year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derrick White College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/derrick-white-1.html |access-date=November 7, 2020 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=November 13, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201113100653/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/derrick-white-1.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

White was selected 29th overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. He was traded to the Celtics in February 2022, becoming a key contributor when they reached the [[2022 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rohlin |first=Melissa |date=June 5, 2022 |title=NBA Finals 2022: Celtics found a hero in Derrick White |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nba/nba-finals-2022-celtics-found-a-hero-in-derrick-white |access-date=March 10, 2024 |website=Fox Sports}}</ref> White became a starter in the [[2022–23 Boston Celtics season|2022–23 season]] and was selected to his first [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] that season and his second the following season. White won his first NBA championship when the Celtics defeated the [[2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]] in five games during the [[2024 NBA Finals]]. White also won a gold medal as a member of the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 U.S. Olympic team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/derrick-white_1954724 |title=WHITE Derrick |work=[[Paris 2024 Olympics]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007200618/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/derrick-white_1954724 |archive-date=October 7, 2024}}</ref>

==High school career==
White attended [[Legend High School]], a brand-new high school in [[Parker, Colorado]], and was a part of its first graduating class.<ref name="relishes">{{cite news |url=https://gazette.com/sports/derrick-white-relishes-chance-to-be-honored-at-legend-where-basketball-career-took-flight/article_5c05a828-ae2b-11ed-9630-0f8ed67f3e24.html |title=Derrick White relishes chance to be honored at Legend where basketball career took flight |work=[[The Gazette (Colorado Springs)|The Gazette]] |first=Luke |last=Zahlmann |date=February 17, 2023 |access-date=May 28, 2023}}</ref> As a freshman on the basketball team, he played with 11 other freshmen en route to a victory in league play.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/05/08/sports/derrick-white-celtics/ |title=Derrick White has always bet on himself. Finally, it's paying off. |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |first=Nicole |last=Yang |date=May 9, 2023 |access-date=May 28, 2023}}</ref> As a senior, White averaged 17.1 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.1 assists, and 2.1 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1628401/derrick-white/rotowire |title=Derrick White {{!}} Player bio|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=May 28, 2023}}</ref>

White scored over 1,000 points in his career.<ref name=relishes/> At the time of his graduation in 2012, White was a six-foot combo guard. In February 2023, he was honored as the first-ever Legend Hall of Fame inductee.<ref name=relishes/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/derrick-white-returning-legend-high-school-parker/ |title=Derrick White returns to old high school: "When I'm done hoopin' I'm going to be back here because Colorado means a lot to me" |work=[[CBS News Colorado]] |first=Eric |last=Christensen |date=February 20, 2023 |access-date=May 28, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
White was lightly recruited out of high school, receiving no scholarship offers from any four-year institutions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |date=June 4, 2022 |title=Derrick White started as the ultimate underdog in his journey to the NBA Finals |url=https://andscape.com/features/derrick-white-started-as-the-ultimate-underdog-in-his-journey-to-the-nba-finals/ |access-date=May 2, 2024 |website=Andscape |language=en-US}}</ref> At the time of his high school graduation, which fell about two months before his 18th birthday, White was barely {{convert|6|ft|sigfig=3|spell=in}} tall—after growing {{convert|2|in|cm}} as a senior.<ref name="Bright spot">{{cite news |title=Derrick White A Bright Spot In Probable Lost Season For Buffs |url=http://denver.cbslocal.com/2017/03/07/derrick-white-university-colorado-buffaloes/ |access-date=May 6, 2017 |work=denver.cbs.local.com |date=March 7, 2017 |archive-date=September 29, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170929215506/http://denver.cbslocal.com/2017/03/07/derrick-white-university-colorado-buffaloes/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The only head coach at a four-year school who showed sustained interest in White was Jeff Culver, then the head coach at the Denver campus of [[Johnson & Wales University]], a non-scholarship [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] member better known for its culinary program. By the time White was preparing to make his college decision, Culver was hired as head coach at [[NCAA Division II]]'s [[UCCS Mountain Lions#Basketball|Colorado–Colorado Springs]] and offered White a room-and-board stipend for his freshman season.<ref name=Eisenberg>{{cite web |url=https://www.yahoo.com/sports/news/colorados-derrick-white-went-unrecruited-unlikely-nba-prospect-170715016.html |title=How Colorado's Derrick White went from unrecruited to unlikely NBA prospect |first=Jeff |last=Eisenberg |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |date=May 8, 2017 |access-date=May 9, 2017 |archive-date=March 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325183146/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/colorados-derrick-white-went-unrecruited-unlikely-nba-prospect-170715016.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

Culver only expected White to become a starter late in his college career. He was aware that White's father had a late growth spurt in college, and also knew that doctors had projected White to potentially reach {{convert|6|ft|5|in}}.<ref name="Eisenberg"/> As it turned out, White nearly reached that potential height by the time he enrolled at Colorado–Colorado Springs, falling just {{convert|1|in|cm}} short.<ref name="Bright spot"/> With his newfound size and athleticism, White became a star at UCCS, starting every game of his three-year career and left as the school's career leader in points (1,912) and assists (343). As a junior, White averaged 25.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 5.2 assists for the Mountain Lions, leading the team to the [[2015 NCAA Division II men's basketball tournament|2015 NCAA tournament]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Jhabvala |first=Nicki |title=Derrick White, a 3-year standout guard at UCCS, transfers to Colorado |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2015/04/19/derrick-white-a-3-year-standout-guard-at-uccs-transfers-to-colorado/ |access-date=May 6, 2017 |work=[[Denver Post]] |date=April 19, 2015 |archive-date=February 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226170442/https://www.denverpost.com/2015/04/19/derrick-white-a-3-year-standout-guard-at-uccs-transfers-to-colorado/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He was named an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derrick White - Men's Basketball |url=https://gomountainlions.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/derrick-white/360 |access-date=May 2, 2024 |website=UCCS Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

Following his junior season, White opted to transfer to Division I [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]] to play for [[Tad Boyle]] and test his skills in the [[Pac-12 Conference]], one of the top conferences in the country.<ref>{{cite news |last=Barnhouse |first=Wendell |title=How former DII All-American Derrick White became Colorado's 'best player' |url=https://www.fanragsports.com/cbb/former-dii-american-derrick-white-became-colorados-best-player/ |access-date=May 6, 2017 |work=fanragsports.com |date=December 21, 2016}}{{Dead link|date=November 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> After sitting out the 2015–16 season per [[NCAA]] rules, White excelled in his lone season with the Buffaloes, averaging 18.1 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game. White was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and a member of the five-man All-Defensive team.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rooney |first=Pat |title=Derrick White's lone season with CU Buffs reaps All-Pac-12, All-Defensive team honors |url=http://www.dailycamera.com/sports/ci_30839168/cu-buffs-derrick-white-named-all-pac-12?source=rss |access-date=May 6, 2017 |work=[[Daily Camera]] |date=March 6, 2017 |archive-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114060624/http://www.dailycamera.com/sports/ci_30839168/cu-buffs-derrick-white-named-all-pac-12?source=rss |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===San Antonio Spurs (2017–2022)===
[[File:Derrick White Spurs.jpg|thumb|White in 2019|274x274px]]
White was one of 60 NBA prospects invited to the 2017 [[NBA draft combine]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Rooney |first=Pat |title=Derrick White to represent CU at NBA draft combine |url=http://www.buffzone.com/mensbasketball/ci_30955305/derrick-white-represent-cu-buffs-at-nba-draft |access-date=May 6, 2017 |work=buffzone.com |date=April 29, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327161243/http://www.buffzone.com/mensbasketball/ci_30955305/derrick-white-represent-cu-buffs-at-nba-draft |archive-date=March 27, 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He was one of only 15 combine invitees who had not been [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] top-150 prospects in high school, and one of only three who did not sign with Division I programs out of high school. In addition, according to [[Yahoo! Sports]] writer Jeff Eisenberg, White was also "the only one who will use part of his first NBA contract to pay off student loans he accumulated paying for tuition at UCCS as a freshman."<ref name=Eisenberg/>

The [[San Antonio Spurs]] drafted White with the 29th pick of the [[2017 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Julian |first=M. |date=June 23, 2017 |title=SPURS SELECT DERRICK WHITE AND JARON BLOSSOMGAME IN 2017 NBA DRAFT |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-select-derrick-white-and-jaron-blossomgame-2017-nba-draft |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111045738/https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-select-derrick-white-and-jaron-blossomgame-2017-nba-draft |archive-date=January 11, 2021 |access-date=June 23, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He was later included in the Spurs' [[2017 NBA Summer League]] roster.<ref>{{cite web |last=Julian |first=M. |date=June 30, 2017 |title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2017 UTAH SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2017-utah-summer-league-roster/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191227173850/https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2017-utah-summer-league-roster |archive-date=December 27, 2019 |access-date=June 30, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On July 6, 2017, White signed with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Schad |first=Matt |date=July 6, 2017 |title=SPURS SIGN 2017 FIRST ROUND PICK DERRICK WHITE |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-2017-first-round-pick-derrick-white/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170717022731/http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-2017-first-round-pick-derrick-white |archive-date=July 17, 2017 |access-date=July 6, 2017 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2022–present)===

==== 2021–22 season: First NBA Finals appearance ====
On February 10, 2022, White was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Josh Richardson]], [[Romeo Langford]], a 2022 first-round pick (which turned into [[Blake Wesley (basketball)|Blake Wesley]]), and the rights to swap 2028 first-round picks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-derrick-white-spurs |website=NBA.com |title=Celtics Acquire Derrick White From Spurs |access-date=February 10, 2022 |date=February 10, 2022 |archive-date=February 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211040200/https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-derrick-white-spurs |url-status=live}}</ref> He made his Celtics debut the following day against the [[Denver Nuggets]] and finished the 108–102 victory with 15 points, six rebounds, two assists, and a steal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 11, 2022 |title=Tatum scores 24, Celtics beat Denver for 7th straight win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401360661 |access-date=February 12, 2022 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

During Game 6 of the [[2022 NBA playoffs|Eastern Conference Finals]] against the [[Miami Heat]] on May 27, White scored 22 points on 7-for-14 shooting, alongside five assists, three steals, and a block in a 111–103 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Heat vs Boston Celtics May 27, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/mia-vs-bos-0042100306/box-score |access-date=2022-05-30 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Celtics would go on to eliminate the Heat in seven games, earning White his first NBA Finals appearance in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boston Celtics vs Miami Heat May 29, 2022 Game Summary {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-mia-0042100307 |access-date=2022-05-30 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In Game 1 of the [[2022 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] on June 2, White had 21 points, three assists, and a rebound during a 120–108 comeback victory over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtics vs. Warriors score: Jaylen Brown, Al Horford lead Boston to upset victory in Game 1 vs. Golden State |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/celtics-vs-warriors-score-jaylen-brown-al-horford-lead-boston-to-upset-victory-in-game-1-vs-golden-state/live/ |access-date=June 2, 2022 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> The Celtics went on to lose the series in six games despite a 2–1 lead.<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 17, 2022 |title=Warriors beat Celtics 103-90 to win 4th NBA title in 8 years |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401442535 |access-date=June 18, 2022 |work=ESPN |location=Boston |agency=The Associated Press}}</ref>

==== 2022–23 season: Transition to starter ====
[[File:Derrick White 2023.png|thumb|White in 2023|357x357px]]
White began the season as a starter for the Celtics. On February 10, 2023, against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], he scored a career-high 33 points in a 127–116 victory.<ref>{{cite news |last=Dudek |first=Greg |title=Celtics Wrap: Derrick White's Career Night Fuels Boston's 3-Point Party |url=https://nesn.com/2023/02/celtics-wrap-derrick-whites-career-night-fuels-bostons-3-point-party/ |work=NESN.com |date=February 11, 2023}}</ref> Three days later, White was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week after averaging 24.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 7.5 assists as a starter in place of the injured [[Marcus Smart]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA recognizes Derrick White for recent hot streak |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/celtics-derrick-white-named-nba-eastern-conference-player-week |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=RSN |date=February 13, 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

White started in 70 games and appeared in all 82 regular season games, both career highs. He also shot 38.1 percent from three and 87.5 percent from the free throw line, while registering 76 blocked shots (all career highs).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derrick White All-time Blocks |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=derrick+white+all-time+blocks |access-date=May 8, 2024 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref> In May, White was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive second team]] for the first time in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jaren Jackson Jr. headlines 2022-23 Kia NBA All-Defensive teams |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-23-all-defensive-teams-announced |access-date=May 9, 2023 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

In Game 6 of the [[2023 NBA playoffs|Eastern Conference Finals]] on May 27, White had 11 points, six assists, four rebounds, three blocks, and a steal while making a [[Buzzer beater|buzzer-beating]] put-back shot as time expired to narrowly defeat the [[Miami Heat]] 104–103 to force a Game 7 in Boston, saving the Celtics from elimination.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/celtics-news-derrick-white-forces-game-7-with-last-second-tip-vs-heat |title=WATCH: Celtics' Derrick White forces Game 7 with season-saving tip-in at the buzzer vs Heat |website=ClutchPoints |last=Songco |first=Paolo |date=May 27, 2023 |access-date=May 27, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2023 |title=Derrick White hits tip-in at buzzer, Celtics force Game 7 against Heat with unbelievable win |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/derrick-white-hits-tip-in-at-buzzer-celtics-force-game-7-against-heat-with-unbelievable-win/ |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Robb |first=Brian |date=May 28, 2023 |title=Celtics beat Heat in Game 6 thriller after Derrick White game winner |url=https://www.masslive.com/celtics/2023/05/celtics-beat-heat-in-game-6-thriller-after-derrick-white-game-winner.html |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=masslive.com |language=en}}</ref> He became the second player in NBA history to hit a buzzer-beating game-winner with his team trailing and facing elimination, joining [[Michael Jordan]]'s "[[The Shot (Bulls–Cavaliers)|The Shot]]" in [[1989 NBA playoffs|1989]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Goss |first=Nick |title=Derrick White joins Michael Jordan as only players to achieve this NBA playoff feat |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/derrick-white-joins-michael-jordan-050334449.html |website=sports.yahoo.com |date=May 28, 2023 |access-date=May 28, 2023}}</ref> Two days later, the Celtics went on to lose Game 7 103–84, where White had 18 points, two rebounds, an assist, and a steal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jimmy Butler, Caleb Martin lead Heat past Celtics in Game 7 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/jimmy-butler-caleb-martin-lead-heat-past-celtics-in-game-7 |website=NBA.com |date=May 30, 2023 |access-date=May 30, 2023}}</ref>

==== 2023–24 season: First NBA championship ====
White remained a starter after [[Marcus Smart]] was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the offseason. White's production increased as he averaged 15.2 points, 5.2 assists, and 4.2 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derrick White 2023-24 Stats per Game - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3078576/type/nba/year/2024 |access-date=June 19, 2024 |website=ESPN}}</ref> White appeared in 73 games (all starts) and shot 46.1 percent from the field, including a career-high 39.6 percent from three.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derrick White Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whitede01.html |access-date=May 8, 2024 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On March 18, 2024, White recorded his first career triple-double with 22 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 119–94 victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/celtics-news-derrick-white-first-career-triple-double-teammates-boston-fans-hyped |title=Derrick White's first career triple-double has teammates, Celtics fans hyped |website=ClutchPoints |last=Sampson |first=Peter |date=March 18, 2024 |access-date=March 18, 2024}}</ref>

During Game 4 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs#(1) Boston Celtics vs. (8) Miami Heat|first round of the playoffs]] against the [[Miami Heat]] on April 29, 2024, White had a playoff career-high 38 points, four rebounds, three assists, and three blocks in a 102–88 road victory.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Krivitsky |first=Bobby |url=https://www.si.com/nba/celtics/derrick-white-stars-porzingis-exits-celtics-push-heat-to-brink-of-elimination |title=Derrick White Stars, Porzingis Exits, Celtics Push Heat to Brink of Elimination |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 29, 2024 |access-date=April 30, 2024}}</ref> During Game 4 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs|Eastern Conference Finals]] against the [[Indiana Pacers]] on May 27, he scored 22 points on 7-for-14 shooting, alongside five steals, four rebounds, four assists, and three blocks while making the game-winning three-pointer as the Celtics completed a 105–102 comeback victory and advanced to the NBA Finals for the second time in three years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greene |first=Rob |date=May 28, 2024 |title=Derrick White Discusses Second May 27 Game-Winner, Sending Celtics to Finals: 'Pretty Good Day' |url=https://www.si.com/nba/celtics/top-stories/derrick-white-discusses-second-may-27-game-winner-sending-celtics-to-finals-pretty-good-day-01hz017g0ggb |access-date=May 29, 2024 |website=Inside The Celtics |language=en-US}}</ref> White helped the Celtics win the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], where they defeated the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in five games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |date=June 17, 2024 |title=Celtics stomp Mavs, clinch record 18th NBA title |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40375053 |access-date=June 18, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2024–25 season: Contract extension ====
[[File:Celtics at Wizards 2024-12-036 (White).jpg|thumb|White in 2024|328x328px]]
On July 1, 2024, a day before his 30th birthday, White signed a four-year, $125.9 million extension with the Celtics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2024 |title=Sources: Celtics, Derrick White agree to $126M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40474465/celtics-derrick-white-agree-126m-extension |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On March 5, 2025, White scored a career-high 41 points in addition to recording three steals, three rebounds, two assists, and a block in a 128–118 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as he and [[Payton Pritchard]] became the first Celtics teammates to make nine or more three-pointers in the same game (Pritchard had 10) and the first to score 40 or more points in the same game (Pritchard had 43).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rights |first=Bird |date=March 5, 2025 |title=Pritchard and White combine for 84 points, Celtics beat Trail Blazers 128-118 |url=https://www.celticsblog.com/2025/3/5/24378827/payton-pritchard-derrick-white-combine-84-points-boston-celtics-beat-portland-trail-blazers-128-118 |access-date=March 6, 2025 |website=CelticsBlog |language=en}}</ref> They are also the first NBA teammates to score 19 three-pointers in a single game, and the first to have at least 40 points and seven three-pointers each.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 6, 2025 |title=Celtics' Payton Pritchard, Derrick White combine for 84 points, set multiple NBA records in Boston win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/celtics-payton-pritchard-derrick-white-combine-for-84-points-set-multiple-nba-records-in-boston-win/ |access-date=March 6, 2025 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> On March 31 against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], White had 14 points, eight rebounds, and 10 assists in the 117–103 victory while setting the Celtics franchise record with the most three-pointers in a season, with 246.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stinar |first=Ben |date=April 1, 2025 |title=Derrick White Made Boston Celtics History Against Grizzlies |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/derrick-white-made-boston-celtics-history-against-grizzlies-nba-news |access-date=April 21, 2025 |website=Fastbreak On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the season playing and starting in 76 games, marking the first time White started in every game he played during his career as he averaged 16.4 points, 4.8 assists, and 4.5 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Derrick White 2024-25 Stats per Game - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3078576/derrick-white |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

During Game 1 of the [[2025 NBA playoffs#(2) Boston Celtics vs. (7) Orlando Magic|first round of the playoffs]] against the [[Orlando Magic]], White led the Celtics in scoring with 30 points while also recording four rebounds, two assists, and two blocks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2025 |title=Derrick White scores 30, Tatum stays in game after fall and Celtics beat Magic 103-86 in Game 1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401767822 |access-date=April 21, 2025 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> In Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals on May 14, he had 34 points, three blocks, three rebounds, and two assists as the Celtics defeated the [[New York Knicks]] 127–102 to force a Game 6 in New York, saving the Celtics from elimination.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 14, 2025 |title=White scores 34 to help Celtics stave off elimination with 127-102 Game 5 win over Knicks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401769750 |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> The Celtics went on to lose the series in six games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/celtics-knicks-takeaways-game-6-2025-nba-playoffs|title=Celtics-Knicks: 5 takeaways as New York ousts Boston to advance to East Finals|website=nba.com|last=Schuhmann|first=John|date=May 17, 2025|access-date=December 31, 2025}}</ref>

==== 2025–26 season: First All-Defensive First Team selection ==== 
On December 30, 2025, White had 27 points, seven rebounds, six assists, and a career-high seven blocks in a 129–119 victory over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2025 |title=Derrick White has 27 points and 7 blocks to lead Celtics past Jazz 129-119 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401810314 |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> His seven blocks tied [[George Gervin]], [[Dennis Johnson]], [[Doug Christie]], and [[Tracy McGrady]] for the most recorded in a game by a guard in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/boston-celtics/celtics-news-derrick-white-left-speechless-making-bonkers-block-history|title=Celtics’ Derrick White left speechless after making bonkers block history|website=ClutchPoints|last=Brown|first=Malik|date=December 31, 2025|access-date=December 31, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar-post-20251230-derrick-white-silences-jazz-with-historic-shot-blocking-effort|title=Derrick White Silences Jazz with Historic Shot-Blocking Effort|website=nba.com|last=Snow|first=Taylor|date=December 30, 2025|access-date=December 31, 2025}}</ref> 

On March 3, 2026, the NBA announced that White had been named the Eastern Conference Defensive Player of the Month for February.<ref>{{Citeweb|url=https://x.com/NBAPR/status/2028915824551956831|title=NBA Communications on X|publisher=[[Twitter]]|quote=San Antonio Spurs forward-center Victor Wembanyama and Boston Celtics guard Derrick White have been named the Kia NBA Western and Eastern Conference Defensive Players of the Month, respectively, for games played in February.|date=March 3, 2026|accessdate=March 3, 2026}}</ref> On April 23, he was named as the recipient of the [[NBA Sportsmanship Award]] for the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtics' Derrick White wins NBA's Sportsmanship Award|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48571872/celtics-derrick-white-wins-nba-sportsmanship-award|access-date=June 19, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On May 22, White was named to his first [[NBA All-Defensive First Team]], while averaging career-highs of 1.1 steals and 1.3 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kia All-Defensive Teams, NBA Social Justice Champion revealed live on Peacock |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-26-all-defensive-teams-announced |website=NBA.com |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=May 22, 2026 |access-date=May 22, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
On August 24, 2019, White was included in the [[2019 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|US national team]]'s final roster for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2019/08/mnt-wc-team-named.aspx |title=2019 USA Basketball Men's World Cup Team Roster Announced |date=August 24, 2019 |website=usab.com |access-date=August 24, 2019 |archive-date=August 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190824162531/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2019/08/mnt-wc-team-named.aspx |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 10, 2024, White was chosen as a member of the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team]] as part of the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics]] in [[Paris]]. Team USA was in need of a replacement player for [[Kawhi Leonard]], who withdrew from the roster that same day.<ref name=windhorst_07102024>{{cite web |first=Brian |last=Windhorst |title=Kawhi Leonard out for Paris Olympics; Derrick White to Team USA |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/40533195/kawhi-leonard-withdraws-team-usa-paris-olympics |website=ESPN |date=July 10, 2024 |access-date=July 11, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first1=Shams |last1=Charania |first2=Joe |last2=Vardon |title=Kawhi Leonard out for Team USA in Olympics, Derrick White to take his place |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5629094/2024/07/10/kawhi-leonard-out-usa-olympics-team/ |access-date=July 11, 2024}}</ref> Throughout the tournament, White averaged 3.8 points, 1.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists, 1.4 steals, and 1 block per game.<ref name="Yahoo">{{cite web |last1=Hayes |first1=Oliver |title=Colorado legend Derrick White wins gold medal at Paris Olympics |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/colorado-legend-derrick-white-wins-232847783.html |website=Yahoo Sports |date=August 10, 2024 |access-date=August 20, 2024}}</ref> He helped the team win the gold medal.<ref name="CNN">{{cite web |last1=Feldscher |first1=Kyle |title=Team USA wins the gold medal in men's basketball, defeating France in a thriller |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/08/10/sport/usa-basketball-wins-gold-medal/index.html |website=CNN |date=August 10, 2024 |access-date=August 20, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
White married Hannah Schneider in August 2021.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 24, 2019 |title=Who is Derrick White's wife Hannah Schneider and when did they get married |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/who-derrick-white-s-wife-hannah-schneider-get-married |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=sportskeeda.com}}</ref> Their first son, Hendrix James, who is named for [[Jimi Hendrix]], was born on May 19, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |last=Levin |first=Jake |date=May 19, 2022 |title=Derrick White shares photo of newborn son |url=https://www.nbcsportsboston.com/nba/boston-celtics/derrick-white-shares-photo-of-newborn-son-following-celtics-win/254622 |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=nbcsports.com}}</ref> Their second son, Daxton, was born on November 4, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fuller |first=Ethan |date=November 7, 2023 |title=Celtics' Derrick White, wife Hannah welcome second child |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/11/07/sports/derrick-white-child |access-date=December 26, 2023 |website=bostonglobe.com}}</ref>

In September 2024, White was attending a [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]] vs. [[Colorado State Rams football|Colorado State]] football game in [[Fort Collins]] when a fan struck him in the back of the head.<ref>{{cite web | last=Phillips | first=Ryan | title=Derrick White Hit in Head During Altercation At Colorado-Colorado State Game | website=SI | date=2024-09-17 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/derrick-white-hit-in-head-altercation-colorado-colorado-state-game | access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref>

==Endorsements==
White has endorsement deals with the Boston-based beverage companies [[Samuel Adams (beer)|Samuel Adams]] and Culture Pop, and has appeared in commercials and on billboards advertising these brands.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gerber |first=Dana |date=June 4, 2024 |title=How Derrick White became a go-to spokesman for Boston-area brands |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/06/04/business/celtics-derrick-white-culture-pop-samuel-adams-endorsement |access-date=June 19, 2024 |publisher=[[The Boston Globe]]}}</ref>
